I will keep my land mostly in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation, because in Quzhou that is still the steadiest way for me to get grain and cash without taking too much market risk. Our rainfall comes mainly in summer, so maize matches the season well, and wheat is still worth planting if I control water and fertilizer carefully. I will not spread myself across too many crops. At my age, I would rather keep the plan simple, mechanized, and predictable. I will also keep a small piece in peanuts, because they sell decently, use less water than wheat, and help break the continuous wheat-maize pattern a little.

For management, I will use improved or hybrid seed, not old saved seed, because I want stable emergence and better resistance. On wheat land I will plough after the previous crop, return straw where possible, sow on time, and give fertilizer in split applications with nitrogen emphasized but not pushed too hard. Wheat will get more irrigation because spring here is dry. After wheat harvest, I will go straight into summer maize with no-tillage or very light tillage to save time and moisture. Maize will get one base fertilizer plus one topdressing, and I will watch for armyworm, corn borer, aphids, and common leaf diseases. On the peanut plot I will use moderate fertilizer, fewer irrigations, and fewer pesticide sprays than grain land. My goal is steady yield, lower risk, and manageable labor, not chasing the highest possible output.
